chunks: we have come out to Thee from under the curtains and coverings (of houses) when the beasts and children are crying, seeking Thy Mercy, hoping for the generosity of Thy bounty and fearing Thy chastisement and retribution.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for rain in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This supplication, often recited by Imam Ali (AS) during rain prayers, vividly captures the communal transition from domestic confinement to public worship, highlighting the psychological tension between hope (rajā’) and fear (khawf). It reflects the Shia emphasis on humility before God’s sovereignty over nature, framing rain not merely as a meteorological event but as a divine mercy responding to sincere repentance and reliance on the Almighty.
